title: Banteay Srei
source: Two ordinary tower/moat photographs and pinned standard PMTiles/Mapzen inputs.
axis: +X east toward the main approach;+Y up;+Z south along the three-tower row.

reconstruction.scope: Banteay Srei medium-fi surviving exterior: three stepped pink-sandstone sanctuary towers and lotus finials, recessed/false doors with curved pediments, eastern mandapa, two corbel-roofed libraries, inner gateways, lower outer/approach gateway remains and concentric stone/laterite enclosure traces. Native map moat and paths remain independent. Fine narrative sculpture, individual carved figures and exact damage inventories are not reproduced.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Photographic proportions estimate central tower11.2m and flanking towers9.8m above their bases; libraries and gateways4–6m, lower outer ruins1–3m. Heights and individual ornament are not measured. The map controls the central envelope, moat and approach, not exact shrine partitions.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: SourceY0 is the retained standard Mapzen sample at the raw anchor. Individual plinths use their local coarse grade with retaining foundations. The common platform is an approximate graded stone terrace. Original ground and native moat water stay intact; exact archaeological floors and seasonal water levels are not surveyed.
